cells.value: Operating — NAERLS (federal extension agency under FMAFS, at ABU Zaria) has run a dedicated e-Extension department since January 2017, operating the National Farmers Helpline call centre (Hausa/Igbo/Yoruba/English, nationwide with zonal offices, weekday service, inbound/outbound calls + SMS) plus web portal and apps. Separately, the World Bank ACReSAL-funded Digital Precision Agricultural Extension (DPAE) voice-advisory platform (automated Hausa voice calls, operated by Precision Development/PxD) reached ~20,000 farmers across 8 northern states in 2025 dry-season trials and entered a Build-Operate-Transfer handover to FMAFS's Department of Agricultural Extension Services in June 2026.
cells.source_title: FMINO official release: FMAFS and ACReSAL Partner with World Bank to Transition DPAE Platform (4 Jun 2026)
cells.quality_evidence: Institutionalisation: standing e-Extension department inside NAERLS since Jan 2017 (naerls.gov.ng/e-extension); NFHL runs with published phone lines, four languages and zonal offices (naerls.gov.ng/nfhl). DPAE transition is an explicit sustainability plan — government extension officers trained to take over database management, phone system operation and audio production under a BOT model; Director of Agricultural Extension Services states the platform 'becomes fully institutionalized within our national extension system' (fmino.gov.ng, 4 Jun 2026). Funding: DPAE is World Bank-financed via ACReSAL; no published budget line found for NAERLS e-extension itself.
cells.scale_evidence: DPAE: ~20,000 farmers reached, 8 states (Kano, Niger, Adamawa, Sokoto, Bauchi, Gombe, Kaduna, FCT), 6 value chains (maize, sorghum, tomato, groundnut, cowpea, rice) — T3, fmino.gov.ng. NFHL: nationwide mandate but NO published call/user volumes. Extension-agent ratio: NOT verifiable — NAERLS APS 2025 release (7 Oct 2025) publishes production data but no ratio; circulating figures span 1:5,000 to 1:10,000 (worst-case 1:24,000) with no resolvable primary source.
cells.search_trail: T3 first for presence: naerls.gov.ng/e-extension and /nfhl (read); fmino.gov.ng DPAE release (read); naerls.gov.ng APS-2025 release (read — no ratio). T2: Heliyon/PMC study on ICT use in SW Nigeria extension noted as context. T4/T5 ratio claims (Guardian, ICIR, MSU CANR) not admissible for a number. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: (1) The bundle guidance embedded an unverifiable number — extension ratio '1:6446' could not be traced to any resolvable source; ICIR quotes a NAERLS-linked director saying Nigeria lacks reliable data on extension-worker numbers. Guidance numbers should carry citations. (2) Ladder ambiguity: does a donor-funded, NGO-operated platform mid-transfer (DPAE) count as 'extension system digitization', or only after the BOT completes? Recorded as Operating with the transfer status stated.
cells.notes: Divergence from prior: prior was assessor-judged 'present but narrow, reach unquantified' — this run upgrades the record to Documented/T3 with a quantified scale rung (DPAE 20k farmers) and named institutional home. Divergence from guidance: 1:6,446 ratio unverified (see protocol_issues).

cells.value: Absent as a standing unit — FMAFS's official published structure (11 service departments, 12 technical departments, 3 units) names no digital, ICT, data, e-agriculture or AI department or unit. Digital-agriculture functions are hosted in projects and partner arrangements instead: the National Digital Farmers Registry under the FG–IFAD Digital Innovation Action Plan with NIMC (Nov 2025); the DPAE advisory platform under the Department of Agricultural Extension Services via World Bank ACReSAL (Jun 2026); the AI/satellite National Agro-Productivity System via an OCP Africa/Ground Truth Analytics partnership (Jul 2026).
cells.quality_evidence: No unit exists to assess. Nearest institutional anchor: Department of Agricultural Extension Services is the named receiving department for DPAE (fmino.gov.ng, 4 Jun 2026); the farmer-registry release (agriculture.gov.ng, 20 Nov 2025) names external partners (IFAD, NIMC, Heifer, ONSA) but no internal digital unit, staffing or budget.
cells.search_trail: T3 first: agriculture.gov.ng/structure/ read in full — no digital/ICT/AI unit among 26 named departments/units (agriculture.gov.ng/departments/ returns 404); agriculture.gov.ng registry release read — no unit named; fmino.gov.ng DPAE release read — responsibility sits with Dept of Agricultural Extension Services. WebSearch for 'FMAFS digital agriculture unit/ICT department' surfaced initiatives (NAPS, DPAE, registry) but no unit. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Definition ambiguity: 'digital/AI unit' — a routine back-office ICT function may exist without appearing on the structure page, and structure-page silence is strong but not conclusive evidence of absence. Recorded Absent on the citable record; recommend a direct FMAFS interview question at country-engagement stage.
cells.notes: RESOLVES the prior desk pass 'Unverified': resolved to Absent on the official record. This substantiates the DELIVERY flag — Nigeria's digital-agriculture delivery capacity is project-hosted (IFAD, World Bank, OCP partnerships), not institutionalised in a staffed, funded ministry unit. Contrast rung: activity is plentiful; the unit is what is missing.

cells.value: Operating (generic digital-talent pipeline; agtech-specific bridging undocumented) — the federal 3MTT (3 Million Technical Talent) programme, run by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy with NITDA since December 2023, trains fellows in 12 tracks including AI/ML, data science, and data analysis & visualisation: Phase 1 selected 30,000 fellows across all 36 states + FCT; Phase 2 plans 270,000 across three cohorts. Data Science Nigeria (private non-profit, est. 2016) runs AI bootcamps and free community AI training. Neither 3MTT, NCAIR, nor DSN documents an agriculture-specific track or ag-AI training programme.
cells.quality_evidence: 3MTT is a federal programme with phased cohort design and nationwide reach, institutionally owned by FMCIDE/NITDA (T3 programme page). NCAIR (NITDA's AI centre) exists with AI infrastructure and the N-ATLaS multilingual LLM project but lists no ag or training-volume specifics on its site. DSN's institutional persistence since 2016 and corporate partnerships (Microsoft, Mastercard) are existence facts from its own site — T5, existence only.
cells.scale_evidence: 3MTT: 30,000 Phase 1 fellows (T3); Phase 2 target 270,000 (60k/90k/120k cohorts) — a target, not delivery. DSN's reach claims ('8M+ learners', '14,000 community members') are unverified vendor statistics — excluded under T5 rules. No agtech-specific training volume is documented anywhere found this run.
cells.search_trail: T3 first: 3mtt.nitda.gov.ng (read), ncair.nitda.gov.ng (read — no ag programmes listed). T5 existence: datasciencenigeria.org (read; statistics excluded). University agtech/ag-data-science programmes: not verifiable this run — WebSearch budget exhausted before a dedicated university-programme query. Accessed 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: T5 boundary case: DSN's own website is the only source for its programmes — admissible for existence only; its reach numbers are excluded. Search-budget exhaustion prevented verifying the prior's claim of university agtech programmes; that sub-claim remains open for loop 2 (candidates: FUNAAB, ABU, LAUTECH agricultural informatics/extension curricula).
cells.notes: Divergence from prior: prior assessor-judged 'University agtech programmes present; scale unverified' — the university half was NOT verified this run and should not be carried forward without a citation. What is now Documented (T3): a large operating generic data-science/AI pipeline with no agtech bridge — the pipeline exists but does not visibly feed agtech.

bundle_issues: 1) The session's shared WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted mid-bundle: 5.12 never received a dedicated search and 5.4/5.8 lost their final sweeps; remaining verification was done via direct WebFetch/Crossref/PDF reads. 5.12's gap is provisional. 2) Two admissible sources were blocked by HTTP 403 (ScienceDirect — the T2 JIA 2026 farmer digital-knowledge article, DOI 10.1016/j.jia.2025.12.056; GSMA AgriTech) — library/API access for loop 2 would resolve both. 3) No Wayback archives were captured for T4/T5 links this run (protocol rule 3) — archiving tooling was not exercised; flag for capture at consolidation. 4) Guidance quality: the bundle guidance embedded an unsourced number (extension ratio '1:6446') that could not be traced to any resolvable source — guidance-supplied figures should carry their citations or be marked as unverified leads. 5) Positive bundle finding: C4's DELIVERY story is now citable end-to-end from T3 sources — no FMAFS digital/AI unit exists (5.7 Absent, resolving the prior Unverified) while digital delivery runs through donor projects (DPAE/ACReSAL, IFAD registry) and a generic non-ag federal talent pipeline (3MTT).
